notes: Hook formulas for X posts. 'match' is a Python regular expression tested case-insensitively against the first non-empty line of a post. Order matters: classifiers (lint.py, hookscore.py, swipe.py, stats.py) take the first formula that matches, so specific formulas come before generic ones. Edit, reorder or add your own. A formula is a starting shape, not a guarantee.

formulas.name: Result + timeframe
formulas.template: I {got a specific result} in {timeframe}. Here's exactly how:
formulas.example: I went from 0 to 4,000 newsletter subscribers in 90 days. Here's exactly how:
formulas.purpose: Leads with proof, so the reader trusts the steps that follow.
formulas.failure_mode: Reads as a brag, or as made up, when the number is round and unverifiable or the steps are generic.

formulas.name: Failure + lesson
formulas.template: I {failed at something specific}. Here's what it taught me:
formulas.example: I lost my biggest client last month. It was my fault, and the fix took one email.
formulas.purpose: Vulnerability earns attention, and a lesson pays it back.
formulas.failure_mode: Humblebrag dressed as failure, or a lesson so vague it could follow any story.
formulas.match: ^\s*i\s+(lost|failed|got fired|got rejected|quit|wasted|burned|blew|almost lost|messed up|screwed up|bombed|was wrong)\b

formulas.name: Before / after
formulas.template: {Time} ago I {bad state}. Today I {good state}.
formulas.example: 2 years ago I couldn't write a tweet without deleting it 5 times. Today I post daily in 10 minutes.
formulas.purpose: A visible gap makes the reader want the bridge between the two states.
formulas.failure_mode: The 'after' sounds like an ad, or there is no bridge in the rest of the post.

formulas.name: Story in a moment
formulas.example: Last Tuesday a stranger replied to my post and offered me a job.
formulas.purpose: Drops the reader into a scene; people finish stories they start.
formulas.failure_mode: Slow scene-setting with no tension in the first line.

formulas.name: Numbered list
formulas.example: 7 free tools I use to write every post on this account:
formulas.purpose: Sets a clear, finite promise; the number tells the reader how much they get.
formulas.failure_mode: Padding the list to hit a number, or items that are generic and unearned.

formulas.name: How I
formulas.example: How I write a week of posts in one 90-minute session:
formulas.purpose: First-person process is more credible than generic advice.
formulas.failure_mode: The 'how' is obvious, or the result is too small to care about.

formulas.name: How to
formulas.example: How to get your first 1,000 followers without posting 5 times a day:
formulas.purpose: Promises a useful outcome and removes the main objection up front.
formulas.failure_mode: Sounds like a blog headline; needs the 'without' clause to stand out.

formulas.name: The mistake
formulas.example: The biggest mistake new freelancers make is pricing by the hour.
formulas.purpose: Loss aversion: readers check whether they are making it.
formulas.failure_mode: Scolding tone, or a 'mistake' everyone already knows about.

formulas.name: Contrarian take
formulas.template: Unpopular opinion: {take that cuts against consensus}.
formulas.example: Unpopular opinion: you don't need a niche for your first 6 months.
formulas.purpose: Disagreement invites replies and signals independent thinking.
formulas.failure_mode: Contrarian for its own sake, or not actually unpopular.
formulas.match: ^\s*(unpopular opinion|hot take|controversial take|hear me out|counterpoint)\b|\b(is|are)\s+(overrated|underrated|a myth|a lie|dead|a scam|wrong)\b

formulas.name: Stop doing
formulas.example: Stop ending every post with 'thoughts?'. Ask one specific question instead.
formulas.purpose: A direct instruction with a replacement is easy to act on.
formulas.failure_mode: Bossy without a reason; the alternative must be concrete.

formulas.name: Warning
formulas.example: Don't sign a client contract until you check these 4 clauses.
formulas.purpose: Protects the reader from a specific, costly outcome.
formulas.failure_mode: Fear-mongering when the risk is small or rare.

formulas.name: The truth about
formulas.example: The uncomfortable truth about going viral: it rarely brings customers.
formulas.purpose: Promises honesty the reader suspects they are not getting elsewhere.
formulas.failure_mode: The 'truth' is a cliche, which breaks the promise immediately.

formulas.name: Nobody talks about
formulas.template: Nobody talks about {overlooked part of a familiar thing}.
formulas.example: Nobody talks about how lonely the first year of freelancing is.
formulas.purpose: Opens a gap between what the reader knows and what they are about to learn.
formulas.failure_mode: Plenty of people do talk about it; readers notice and leave.
formulas.match: \b(nobody|no one|few people|most people don'?t)\s+(talks? about|tells? you|is talking about|mentions?|realizes?|knows?)\b

formulas.name: Surprising stat
formulas.example: 68% of my best-performing posts were under 100 characters.
formulas.purpose: A precise number is concrete and easy to remember.
formulas.failure_mode: Unsourced or invented numbers. Only use data you actually have.

formulas.name: I studied N things
formulas.template: I {analyzed / interviewed / read} {N} {things}. Here's the pattern:
formulas.example: I read 200 cold emails that got replies. 3 patterns showed up again and again:
formulas.purpose: Borrowed authority from effort the reader did not have to spend.
formulas.failure_mode: The effort is fake or the 'pattern' is obvious.

formulas.name: A vs B
formulas.example: Threads vs single posts: what 6 months of my data says.
formulas.purpose: Readers who face the choice self-select in.
formulas.failure_mode: No verdict, or a verdict that is 'it depends'.

formulas.name: Prediction
formulas.example: In 3 years, 'prompt engineer' won't be a job title. Here's what replaces it.
formulas.purpose: Future-facing claims invite debate and replies.
formulas.failure_mode: Unfalsifiable hype with no reasoning behind it.

formulas.name: Audience callout
formulas.template: If you're a {specific audience} who {struggle}, read this.
formulas.example: If you're a designer who hates selling, this is the only script you need.
formulas.purpose: Naming the reader stops the right people and filters the wrong ones.
formulas.failure_mode: The audience is so broad ('if you're a human') it calls out nobody.

formulas.name: Advice to past self
formulas.template: If I were starting {X} today, I'd {do this}:
formulas.example: If I were starting on X today with 0 followers, I'd do these 5 things:
formulas.purpose: Hindsight framing feels earned and practical.
formulas.failure_mode: Advice that only works because of the head start you now have.

formulas.name: Steal this
formulas.example: Steal my 4-line structure for posts that get replies:
formulas.purpose: Promises an immediately usable asset; drives bookmarks.
formulas.failure_mode: The asset is thin, which teaches people to skip your next one.

formulas.name: Named framework
formulas.example: The 3-question framework I use before writing any post:
formulas.purpose: A named, repeatable system feels more valuable than tips.
formulas.failure_mode: Renaming common sense as a 'framework'.

formulas.name: News breakdown
formulas.template: {Company or person} just {did X}. Here's what it means for {audience}:
formulas.example: Acme just raised prices 3x. Here's what small teams should do instead.
formulas.purpose: Rides existing attention and adds your interpretation.
formulas.failure_mode: Restating the news with nothing added, or getting the facts wrong.

formulas.name: Here's why / how
formulas.example: Here's why your posts get views but no followers:
formulas.purpose: Names a problem the reader has and promises the cause.
formulas.failure_mode: Generic; works only if the problem in the line is specific.

formulas.name: Direct question
formulas.template: {Specific question your audience has opinions about}?
formulas.example: What's the one tool you'd keep if you could only keep one?
formulas.purpose: Invites replies directly; works best when anyone in the niche can answer.
formulas.failure_mode: Vague questions ('thoughts?') or ones with an obvious answer.

formulas.name: One-liner
formulas.example: Clarity beats cleverness. Every time.
formulas.purpose: Easy to agree with, easy to repost.
formulas.failure_mode: A fortune-cookie line with nothing behind it.
